 O R D E R
Heard Mr. Shreeyash U. Lalit, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. S.D. Sanjay, learned Additional Solicitor General for the respondent-State.
2. Delay condoned.

3. The petitioner is seeking bail in connection with FIR No. 68 of 2021, registered at Police Station Punjabi Bagh, Delhi, on 21.01.2021, for the commission of offences punishable under Sections 304B/498A/354/323/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
4. The allegation against the petitioner, who is husband of the deceased, is that he was responsible for the death of his wife.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that there is a charge also under Section 304B/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, but from the overall facts and circumstances of the case, it is highly improbable.

He submits that a few days prior to the incident the deceased had made a complaint to the Crime Against Women (CAW) Cell with regard to the atrocities she was facing, and nothing with regard to threat to her life was alleged.
Learned counsel submitted that in the past also, twice she had left the matrimonial home due to some dispute and had returned.

Learned counsel submitted that, at best, for the present, even if it is assumed that the lady had committed suicide and the petitioners conduct may have been one of the reasons for her doing so, the same would still carry a punishment of 10 years and under Section 479 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, an accused would be entitled for consideration of bail if he has undergone more than one-third of the maximum sentence.
6.

It was submitted that since the body of the deceased was found hanging in her maternal home and only ligature mark is under the neck as per the postmortem report, there is very little chance of there being any foul play and that the petitioner deserves to be enlarged on bail having been in custody for a little less than five years.

7. Learned Additional Solicitor General for the respondent-State submitted that the death having occurred in the background of there being past history of discord and also a complaint to the CAW Cell, prima facie the petitioner can be said to be responsible for the death of the deceased.

sentences.text: Having considered the matter and taking an overall view, we are inclined to allow the prayer for bail.
9. Accordingly, the petitioner is directed to be released on bail on such terms and conditions as may be imposed by the trial Court.
10. It goes without saying that one of the conditions shall be that the petitioner shall fully cooperate in the investigation/trial.
11. The Special Leave Petition stands disposed of in the above terms.
12. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.

(POOJA SHARMA) (ANJALI PANWAR)
